title: Sell Mineral Rights in Antelope Hills, WY
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights antelope hills wy
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights Antelope Hills, WY | Natrona Co.
metaDescription: Antelope Hills sits just outside Casper near the historic Salt Creek trend. Get a courthouse-checked read on your Natrona County mineral interest before selling.
heroLead: Antelope Hills is close enough to Casper that I get asked all the time whether it's inside the old Salt Creek field trend. Sometimes yes, sometimes no, and the difference matters a great deal to what your minerals are worth.
intro: Salt Creek was one of the largest oil fields in the country when it was discovered in the early 1900s, and it turned Casper into a refining town almost overnight. Development has spread and contracted around that core for over a century, and Natrona County's records reflect every phase of it, active leases, expired leases, unitized production, and plenty of quiet acreage that's never drawn a permit.
Before I tell you what an Antelope Hills tract is worth, I check exactly where your section sits relative to the producing units still active today, because that's the whole ballgame here.

sections.heading: Salt Creek's long tail
paragraphs: Salt Creek has produced for over a century and still has active waterflood and secondary-recovery operations in parts of the field, which is unusual longevity for a Wyoming asset. If your tract sits inside a currently unitized portion, you may have a real royalty history to price against. If it sits at the trend's edge, it's a different conversation entirely.
I've seen both kinds of ownership come out of the same family estate, split fractions where one heir's quarter section produces and another's, a mile away, never has.

sections.heading: Confirming your position
paragraphs: I pull the Natrona County recorder's records for your specific legal description and check it against the current unit boundaries on file with the Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission. That tells me whether you're inside active production or outside it, which determines whether we're pricing a royalty asset or speculative acreage.

This checking process usually takes me a couple of days once I have your legal description or deed in hand. I'd rather take that time up front than hand you a number that turns out to be wrong once someone actually looks at the paperwork.

faqs.question: Is Antelope Hills inside the Salt Creek unit?
faqs.answer: Depends entirely on your specific section. I'll check your legal description against the current unit boundary before answering.

faqs.question: What if my family's interest has never produced anything?
faqs.answer: That's common even close to Salt Creek. I'll price it as undeveloped acreage and tell you honestly that it's a different category than producing minerals.

faqs.question: How do royalty checks factor into your offer?
faqs.answer: If you're receiving payments, send me a recent statement. Current production numbers are the strongest evidence for pricing a producing interest.

faqs.question: Do you buy small fractional interests?
faqs.answer: Yes, small fractions are common in this area and I quote them the same way as larger tracts, scaled to your actual share.
